heading: Give the extra time a purpose
intro: Before choosing the longer format, name what you hope the additional time will make possible. It might be attention to a particular interest, a gentler rhythm or space between outings. Ask how the actual program supports that purpose. Count dates and nights separately, and keep the complete journey in view so that an extra package day does not obscure extra travel.
points: What specific interest or pacing preference would you like the longer stay to support?
How many accommodation nights and full activity hours appear in the actual five-day proposal?
Which additional services or travel arrangements sit outside the quoted package?

heading: Day 1: understand the whole stay
intro: Arrival is a chance to understand how the coming days fit together. Confirm the transfer and meal arrangements, then ask about the outline of activities and any choices that need an early decision. Share your pace and interests with the provider before the program begins. Keep optional activities distinct from inclusions so your expectations match the services that have been agreed.
points: What arrival and orientation arrangements are included, and who explains the program to your group?
Which choices need to be made before arrival, and which can be discussed during the stay?
How are changes communicated if an offered activity cannot run as proposed?

heading: Day 2: establish your focus
intro: Use the first main day to begin the interest that drew you to the region. Ask about the offered route, guiding and time at the activity rather than relying on a broad label such as wildlife tour. Discuss the effort and equipment involved. A clear focus also gives you a basis for deciding what to repeat or change later in the stay.
points: Which confirmed outing best introduces your main interest at the property’s actual location?
What experience does the guide bring to that interest, and how large is the activity group?
What effort, equipment and transfer time should your group expect for the proposed outing?

heading: Day 3: discuss flexibility or depth
intro: The middle day can be a deliberate choice rather than another fixed item on a list. Ask whether the provider can offer a different outing, more attention to an interest or time to rest. Clarify what depends on the shared group and what needs a separate arrangement. Choose from confirmed options; an open space in a sample itinerary does not establish availability.
points: Which alternatives can the provider confirm, and what needs advance booking or additional payment?
Can you revisit an interest without requiring the whole shared group to change its program?
What would a slower middle day look like within the services actually included?

heading: Day 4: return to what matters
intro: Make the final main day useful rather than hurried. Review your priorities with the provider and ask which confirmed outing fits the remaining time and your energy. A return to a favorite interest can be more valuable than an unrelated addition. Leave room to prepare for departure and avoid treating the final day as a chance to complete every activity mentioned in a brochure.
points: Which offered activity would you most value before leaving, and what guiding does it require?
Would repeating an outing or choosing a different one better fit your group’s remaining priorities?
Does the plan leave the preparation and rest your group wants before the return journey?

heading: Day 5: close the journey clearly
intro: Connect the final departure to the complete cost and your onward plans. Confirm the last included meal, transfer, drop-off point and the end of the operator’s services. Mark any transport or accommodation you book separately. Keep the contacts and change terms with the itinerary. A longer stay still needs a clear return plan; its duration does not resolve connection questions.
points: Which final-day services are included, and at what point does the operator’s responsibility end?
How does the return connect with your next booking according to the confirmed arrangements?
What exclusions and change terms remain relevant when comparing this stay with a shorter version?
